lines.speaker: ben
lines.text: Every family has its own Christmas traditions.

lines.speaker: ben
lines.text: Some families have peaceful Christmas mornings.

lines.speaker: ben
lines.text: My family? Well... we have this.

lines.speaker: diane
lines.text: Frank, that tree is not going to hold itself!

lines.speaker: frank
lines.text: It's holding, Diane. It's totally holding.

lines.speaker: ben
lines.text: Merry Christmas. Please don't sue us.

lines.speaker: ben
lines.text: I'm Ben. I'm twenty years old, I still believe in Christmas, and I still can't touch the lights.

lines.speaker: diane
lines.text: Ben, those shopping bags are not decorations.

lines.speaker: frank
lines.text: Everything is a decoration if you believe hard enough.

lines.speaker: ben
lines.text: Here's how it works. Mom plans everything. Dad says he's in charge. Max is in charge of trouble. And I'm in charge of telling you about it.

lines.speaker: frank
lines.text: Step one: the stand. Step two: the tree. Step three: victory.

lines.speaker: ben
lines.text: Dad, the stand is upside down.

lines.speaker: ben
lines.text: Dad has never once read the instructions. He says instructions are for people who are scared of their own decorations.

lines.speaker: diane
lines.text: Ham goes in at four. Potatoes at four fifteen. Nobody touches the gravy.

lines.speaker: max
lines.text: Mom, can I have a cookie?

lines.speaker: ben
lines.text: Mom runs the kitchen like an air traffic controller. Dad thinks he's a chef. Max thinks every cookie is already his.

lines.speaker: ben
lines.text: Cookie time. The one part of Christmas where being messy is the goal.

lines.speaker: ben
lines.text: Mom's cookies look like snowflakes. Dad's look like a crime scene. Mine look like the snowflakes' sad cousin.

lines.speaker: max
lines.text: Is this the one where the dog gets lost?

lines.speaker: frank
lines.text: No, this is the one where the train comes back.

lines.speaker: ben
lines.text: The fireplace is not in his eye, Dad.

lines.speaker: max
lines.text: It's just one peek. One tiny peek.

lines.speaker: max
lines.text: I'm not! I'm just shaking it!

lines.speaker: ben
lines.text: He's been shaking that box since Thanksgiving. It's a sweater. It is always a sweater.

lines.speaker: ben
lines.text: Every year we say the same thing. Every year it still feels like magic.

lines.speaker: diane
lines.text: Don't make me say it twice.

lines.speaker: frank
lines.text: Diane, the ham is getting cold.

lines.speaker: ben
lines.text: I used to think Christmas was about the tree and the lights and the presents.

lines.speaker: ben
lines.text: But when I look around this table, I see what matters. It's the people who keep showing up. Even when the tree falls on them.

lines.speaker: max
lines.text: The tree falls on Dad every year.

lines.speaker: frank
lines.text: Once. It falls on me once.

lines.speaker: ben
lines.text: Every year somebody says it's the last Christmas like this.
